title: Install and Verify the .NET SDK
learningObjectives: Explain the difference between the .NET SDK and runtime.
Identify the official .NET download and installation source.
Use dotnet --info and dotnet --list-sdks to inspect an installation.
Verify that a project can be created and built with the selected SDK.
Diagnose common PATH, SDK-selection and target-framework problems.

understand.concept: The .NET SDK is the toolset required to create and build C# projects. A runtime can execute compatible applications but does not provide the complete project-building toolchain. Installing an SDK makes the `dotnet` command available in a terminal, subject to operating-system and PATH configuration.
understand.whyItMatters: A verified SDK gives learners a repeatable environment and allows CI to compile and execute examples rather than relying only on visual code inspection.
understand.analogy: Installing the runtime is like having a device that can operate a finished machine; installing the SDK is like having the tools to build and test the machine too.
understand.analogyLimit: SDK installation alone does not guarantee every project builds. A project may require a different target framework, workload, package feed, native dependency or environment configuration.

explain.narrative:
## Install from the official source

Use Microsoft's official .NET download and installation documentation for your operating system. Prefer a supported SDK version and keep security servicing updates current.

## Verify the command line

Run `dotnet --info` to inspect SDKs, runtimes and environment details. Run `dotnet --list-sdks` to list installed SDK versions and `dotnet --list-runtimes` to list installed runtimes. If the command is not found, check installation completion, terminal restart and PATH configuration.

## Create a verification project

Run `dotnet new console -n FirstCSharpApp`, enter the generated directory, then run `dotnet run`. The template may use top-level statements; later lessons explain both top-level programs and the explicit Main entry point.

## Version policy

CodeSaathi's initial CI baseline is .NET 10 LTS / C# 14. .NET 11 is a newer STS release at the time of this audit; it is not silently substituted for the reproducible LTS baseline.
